gaps.sentence: She has lived in this street ___ 2015.
gaps.hint: starting point of a period up to now
gaps.explanation: 'Since' is used with a point in time when the situation started and continues; 'for' is used with a length of time.

gaps.sentence: Our team has a good ___ of winning on Saturday.
gaps.hint: pattern: have a good ___ of doing something
gaps.explanation: 'Have a chance of doing something' is the standard collocation for the likelihood of success.

gaps.sentence: Teenagers ___ hours every day on social media.
gaps.hint: to use time or money on something (neutral)
gaps.explanation: 'Spend time/money on something' is the neutral verb for using time or money; 'waste' implies useless use.

gaps.sentence: The company ___ its workers' wages by three per cent.
gaps.explanation: 'Raise' is transitive (raise wages); rise is intransitive.

gaps.sentence: One of the screws on the bracket has come ___.
Thousands of people were forced to ___ their homes.
gaps.hint: a verb is needed after 'to'; meaning: abandon
gaps.explanation: 'Desert' is also a verb meaning to abandon; 'dessert' is only the sweet course of a meal.

gaps.sentence: The soup tastes ___ ; add a pinch of salt.
gaps.explanation: 'Bland' = without much taste; the others are unrelated words.

gaps.sentence: She refused on ___ ; she would not bend the rules for anyone.
gaps.explanation: 'On principle' = because of one's moral rules.
